Sessions / Session 03 Scene 02 The Shark

The Shark

→ Run guide opener ends at “the lanterns swing hard to port and stay there.” Continue here.

Starting state: The shark is circling and probing. The barb has not yet seated. Players can act before the hook lands.

Target time: 60–75 minutes. If it runs long, compress aftermath and move to Calveno.

Shark Stat Snapshot

HP: 114 | AC: 15 | Attack bonus: +9 | Speed: swim 60 ft.

AttackHitEffect
Bite22 (3d10+6) piercingGrappled, escape DC 17
Barbed Tail17 (2d10+6) slashingDC 17 Str save or pulled 20 ft; off-vessel means overboard
Hooking DriveActivated on hook seatShip cannot move until tail is freed; pull/drown cycle begins

Blood Frenzy: advantage against any creature below max HP.

Surge: when a creature enters water within 30 ft., shark moves up to 30 ft. and bites if in range. Not an action. State it clearly once when first relevant.

ElementState
SharkCircling port; dorsal fin breaks surface briefly during probing
TailBelow the waterline at all times; hook and joint never visible from deck
ShipListing 5–10 degrees port once hook seats; rail close to water
VisibilityPre-dawn after storm; dim light; nothing visible below the waterline
OverboardDeath pressure; Surge fires immediately

CrewDefault If UndirectedIf Directed

DM Note

Round 2 warning: “Old Faas has a hatchet out at the anchor chain.” Give the party a beat to stop or redirect him.

Run Loop

Each round:

  1. Name the phase. Probing, pulling, drowning, or repositioning.
  2. State the ship consequence. List, hull sound, water, crew movement.
  3. Ask for PC actions.
  4. Use one crew default if no PC redirects that crew member.
  5. Advance the shark. Probe strike, hook attempt, pull, or drown.
  6. Remind the table what changed. Hull worse, breach wider, shark hurt, window open or closed.

Do not track ship HP. Sem is the hull narrator.

Phase Structure

Phase 0 — Probing (Rounds 1–2)

The shark tests the hull with glancing tail strikes. A deep underwater percussion from below the port hull, then the hull shaking. The dorsal fin may break the surface — long, pale, moving too slowly for its size.

Players can act here. Meaningful intervention (significant damage, deterrent, distraction) can delay or prevent the hook seating. Default: if the party does nothing, the hook seats at the end of Round 2.

Pre-Hook OptionResult
Deal 20+ damage during probingShark recoils; no hook attempt this round
Chum, bright light, or loud percussionDC 13 Wis; success delays probe 1 round. Three successes → shark disengages entirely
Thunk’s swivel gun2d6; on 8+, shark skips hook attempt this round

Phase 1 — Hook Seats

Read Aloud

The next impact is different. Not a strike — a catch. The hull groans and doesn’t stop groaning. The list doesn’t correct. From below, Sem starts screaming.

The barb is through the hull, below the waterline, into the hold. The pull begins immediately.

Phase 2 — The Pull

The shark turns and drags. The bow swings hard to port — 30 degrees in a few seconds.

Read Aloud

The bow lurches to port like something enormous grabbed it and yanked. The rigging shrieks. Anyone not holding something goes down.

Mechanic

All PCs and crew on deck: DC 12 Athletics or Acrobatics or fall prone and slide 10 ft. toward port rail. The shark then reverses direction mid-pull — the bow starts to come back, but the hook angle changes, driving the barb deeper.

Phase 3 — The Drown

Read Aloud

The port rail goes under. The bow tilts hard. Water comes over the side in sheets. Then the ship fights back — she’s too light, too full of air. The shark cannot hold her under. The ship hits the waterline like a dropped plank. The hull rings. Something below breaks.

Hull condition (Sem narrates — not HP):

  1. “She can take another one, but not five more.”
  2. “The frames are cracking — she’s breathing water now.”
  3. “One more of those and I can’t keep her up.”

After stage 3: the ship breaks apart if unresolved.

Cycle Reset

After the drown, the shark repositions and begins again: probe → hook attempt → pull → drown → repeat. Each full cycle advances Sem’s hull narration by one stage.

Blood Interruption

If blood enters the water (PC overboard, crew blood washing out through the breach, shark wound) — the shark abandons the pull, moves to the blood source, and spends one round investigating. Hook tension releases temporarily.

Read Aloud

The tension releases. The ship groans back toward level. Somewhere in the dark water, something is moving toward the blood.

DM Note

One round. After it, the shark repositions and re-hooks. This is the player opportunity window.

The Joint

The joint — the scarred seam where the lower lobe begins — is below the waterline, outside the hull. Never visible from the weather deck.

What they can discover:

  • From the hold: the lobe enters through the breached planking below water level; they can touch it, feel it flexing — but the joint is further out, outside the hull, underwater
  • From above deck: the tail disappears into dark water; no visible indication of joint location
  • Perrin’s dream: he knows the joint is roughly 10 ft. along the lobe from the hull, and how deep

Attacking the joint:

  • Over the rail: DC 12 Acrobatics first or fall overboard. Attack at disadvantage from unstable deck. 20+ slashing severs the lobe.
  • Overboard: full access, no disadvantage, but Surge fires immediately. Death pressure.
  • Perrin’s knowledge removes disadvantage on the over-the-rail attack and lets him direct another PC precisely.

Cutting the lobe from inside the hold:

  • Needs 3 successful hits (any damage) or 1 hit dealing 15+
  • Severs the lobe stub from the shark; barb remains wedged in hull but shark is freed
  • Breach widens; Sem screams; shark disengages
DM Note

The designed solution is the joint (easiest sever mechanic), but cutting the lobe from the hold is a real option with a harder threshold. Any physical plan that makes sense gets a roll and a consequence.

Cut lobe from hold3 hits any damage or 1 hit 15+. Severs lobe; barb stays; shark disengages. Breach widens.

Ship Narration

Probing:

  • A low percussion from below the port hull. Not a wave. Regular.
  • The ship rocks to port and doesn’t fully settle before the next one comes.
  • From below: something moving along the hull, slow and heavy.

Hooked / pull:

  • The list deepens hard as the shark drives weight into the hull, then partially corrects.
  • Salt water comes over the port rail in a sheet.
  • Barrels in the hold roll to port and hit the bulkhead together.

Drown:

  • The port rail goes under. It comes back. Everything not lashed is wet.
  • The ship hits the surface hard — not a roll, a strike.
  • From below: a sound like a frame cracking, then Sem’s voice.

When the joint severs:

Read Aloud

The sound is a cannon shot. Not a crack — a percussion, something under enormous tension releasing all at once. The shark recoils hard to port. The tail stub wrenches free from the hull with a grinding tear. Water hits the breach fast for three seconds before Sem gets his brace in. The ship rolls back toward level. The port side goes quiet.

Behavioral Arc

Shark StateBehavior
114–58 HPCommitted; pressing probing hits; hooking and cycling aggressively
57–29 HPTesting escape angles; circling wider; more responsive to deterrents
28 HP or lowerLooking for a reason to disengage; chum, light, pain, or noise can end it
0 HPHard and fast. No body. No confirmation. It may be dead; no one knows.

After It Ends

The fight ends when the shark disengages, is driven off, or dies.

  • Tail stub or barb remains wedged in hull unless the resolution removed it.
  • Sem can keep the ship afloat in calm water, not another storm.
  • The Uncertainty needs dry dock before rough sailing.
  • Move to Scene 03 — Aftermath quickly.
